as_told.title: Urartian cuneiform inscriptions misattribute the ruins

plain: A researcher called Matt tells podcast host Jesse Michels about the Urartians, an ancient people of the Lake Van region in eastern Turkey whom he dates to around 2000 BC, or about 3,000 years ago. He says mainstream archaeology credits them with the ruins, artefacts and symbols there because they carved cuneiform, the ancient wedge-shaped writing, into some temples. Matt suggests instead that they built on much older foundations left by an earlier culture.
